clue.text: Hoopla's mainly@ restricting vital supply

indicators.note: the opening words restrict, or hold in, the run of letters we want, so look inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A fairground hoopla stall is said to be choking off some essential supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood plasma is the fluid carrying cells and nutrients round the body, and donated plasma is a life-saving medical resource.

clue.text: Prune man stewed for a year

indicators.note: stewing mixes things up in the pot, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A man stews prunes, as he does every year.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for each year or annually, used for yearly rates and salaries.

clue.text: Alabama graduate to scrutinize regressive reference works

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word for scrutinize is read from its end

parts.note: scan, to scrutinize, written backwards
a Master of Arts graduate
AL is the US postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: An Alabama graduate pores over old-fashioned books of reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Almanacs are annual publications of calendars, tables and facts consulted for information.

clue.text: Staff keeps nametag that's misprinted, showing core competencies etc

indicators.note: a misprint puts letters in the wrong order, so those words are to be rearranged

parts.note: to man something is to staff it
the letters of both words rearranged

explanation.surface: An employee keeps wearing a badge with a typo, which says much about corporate skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a link meaning 'holds'; it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Core competencies is a typical piece of corporate jargon, an example of the buzzword-laden language bosses use.

clue.text: Something sharp, with soda, knocked back somewhere in W Indies

parts.note: a barb is a sharp point, as on a hook

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but here the words are sent backwards

parts.note: the word soda written backwards

explanation.surface: Someone downs a sharp drink mixed with soda, as one might on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is an island nation in the Caribbean, one of the West Indies group of islands.

clue.text: Space that's less humid, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: less humid means more airy; in a non-rhotic accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: A room described as less muggy than others.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or expanse, a stretch of open space or surface.

clue.text: Dish of leftovers: undercooked mouse stew might do this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British fry-up of yesterday's potato and cabbage

definitions.text: undercooked mouse stew might do this
definitions.note: a pair of verbs describing what the stew and mouse do, not a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a stew simmering makes one noise, and a live mouse in it makes another

explanation.surface: A grim kitchen tale of a stew with a barely cooked mouse in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A stew in the pot bubbles, and a mouse not properly cooked would still squeak.
explanation.definitionFit: The British dish is fried mashed potato and cabbage from the previous day's roast, named for the sounds it makes frying.

clue.text: Frank Capra's job was to do this

definitions.text: Capra's job was to do this
definitions.note: a verb phrase: what a film director does
definitions.meaning: second meaning: what a film director does

explanation.walkthrough: Frank Capra reads as one name, the director of It's a Wonderful Life; split it and Frank is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Direct means plain-spoken and honest, and directing films was the work of the Hollywood director Capra.

clue.text: Nurse, one that's got into habits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a senior nurse in a British hospital ward
second meaning: a nun, who wears the robe called a habit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Got into habits' suggests forming routines; the habits are nuns' robes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a ward's senior nurse is called Sister, and a nun in a religious order is also a sister.

clue.text: 'Vroom', 'mwah', 'nosh' oddly missing in book of Bible

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions go missing, leaving only the even-placed ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on across the three quoted words

explanation.surface: Three slangy noises and words for engines, kisses and food are oddly absent from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's Epistle to the Romans is a New Testament letter, usually just called Romans.

clue.text: In retrospect, playground superb, having banished quiet crazy demonic dog

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word for playground is read backwards

parts.note: a rec (recreation ground) is a public playground

indicators.note: crazy signals that the remaining letters of superb are jumbled
having banished means the letter for quiet is sent out of superb

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Looking back, a fine playground has been ruined by a mad hound once noise was outlawed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retrospect' turns REC to CER. SUPERB 'having banished' P leaves SUERB, and 'crazy' rearranges that to BERUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cerberus is the three-headed hound guarding the gates of Hades, the underworld.

clue.text: Make more attractive posterior: lop off slice at first, then swap sides

indicators.note: then swap sides means the two halves of what is left change places
lop off slice at first means cutting a single letter from the front

parts.note: the posterior is one's rear end

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery advice: trim the backside a little at the front, then switch it round for a better look.
explanation.walkthrough: REAR END after 'lop off slice at first' (its first letter cut) is EAREND; 'then swap sides' makes EAR and END change places.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to make someone liked or loved, winning their affection and so becoming more appealing.

clue.text: Almost no-one sang about geometric figures

indicators.note: about signals the letters being turned around and rearranged
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hardly anybody in the choir was singing about shapes.
explanation.walkthrough: NO-ONE 'Almost' (without its last letter) is NOON; with SANG, 'about' rearranges NOONSANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a polygon with nine sides and nine angles, a plane shape studied in geometry.

clue.text: Briefly hit it off … before he delivers trite observation

indicators.note: before puts the shortened word ahead of he
briefly means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: two people who hit it off are said to click

explanation.surface: A couple got on well for a moment, until he trotted out a hackneyed line.
explanation.walkthrough: CLICK 'Briefly' (cut short) is CLIC, placed 'before' HE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is an overused phrase or idea that has lost its originality, so a banal remark.

clue.text: Prepared communal rice that won't appeal to all

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the anagram fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A shared pot of cooked rice is set out, a dish not everyone will like.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommercial lacks mass-market pull, so it is unlikely to attract a wide paying audience.

clue.text: Reportedly scratched a Monet

indicators.note: something reported is heard spoken, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: scratched means clawed, and the first name sounds the same

explanation.surface: News that a Monet painting has been damaged by scratching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Monet' looks like a painting; it means a person called Monet.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter, so Claude is one member of the Monet family.

clue.text: Plant described by Actinobole and Ericaceae

indicators.note: the outer words draw a line round, describe, the letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the middle one and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A botanical note on a plant characterised by two scientific plant groups.
explanation.walkthrough: Actinobole is an Australian daisy genus and Ericaceae the heather family, real botanical names fitting the plant surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is a poisonous evergreen shrub with pink or white flowers, grown in warm climates.

clue.text: Horrible women love exits being unopened

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: being unopened means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: egresses are ways out, exits

explanation.surface: A romance falls flat when the doors stay shut.
explanation.walkthrough: EGRESSES 'being unopened' loses its first letter to leave GRESSES, after O (love).
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a hideous cruel giantess, so the plural means monstrous females.

clue.text: A land manager ordered hefty bill

indicators.note: put in order means rearranged, so the preceding letters are sorted anew

parts.note: the anagram fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: An estate manager ordered something and ran up a big invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost an arm and a leg is an idiom for being extremely expensive, hence a very large charge.

clue.text: 'Thick Scum' not about to become takeaway staple

parts.note: thick means stupid, dim

indicators.note: not means the letter for about is left out of scum

parts.note: c (circa) is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A murky film of grime somehow turns into a popular dish to go.
explanation.walkthrough: SCUM 'not' having C (circa, about) leaves SUM, after DIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim sum, small Cantonese dumplings and buns, are a mainstay of Chinese takeaway menus.

clue.text: On the radio, noticed a creepy-crawly

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: noticed is spied; in a non-rhotic accent the pair sounds like the creature

explanation.surface: A radio presenter mentions having noticed some bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy-crawly is an informal name for any small crawling creature such as an insect or arachnid.

clue.text: Everyman's quiet, regularly kitschy and rascally

parts.note: the setter Everyman refers to himself: I'm, I am
p for piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: taking letters at a regular interval, every other one, from the next word

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being quiet, somewhat tacky and a bit naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's own name in the clue stands for I or ME; with the possessive it is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish describes playful, mischievous behaviour, like that of a small devil or rascal.

clue.text: Promo: 'Bracket is tolerable!'

parts.note: a promo is an advertisement, or ad
to bracket things together is to treat them as equivalent

explanation.surface: An advertising slogan boasts that a shelf bracket is merely passable.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means good enough or acceptable, satisfactory without being excellent.

clue.text: Glitzy girl losing heart in the morning

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: A sparkly young woman feels deflated at breakfast time.
explanation.walkthrough: GAL 'losing heart' drops its middle A to leave GL, followed by AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Glam is short for glamorous, describing showy, flashy style full of glitter.

clue.text: Without warning, secretive, underground hollow lair invaded

indicators.note: something invaded has others get inside it, so one word wraps the rest

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive

indicators.note: hollowed out means emptied of its middle, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: just its first and last letters
an animal's lair is its den

explanation.surface: A sneaky intruder breaks into a secret subterranean hideout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground hollow' looks like a cave; it is the word underground emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Suddenly means abruptly or unexpectedly, happening with no advance notice.

clue.text: Primarily, very elevated landscapes; dry treeless soil?

definitions.text: Primarily, very elevated landscapes; dry treeless soil?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of each word that follows

parts.words: very elevated landscapes; dry treeless soil
parts.note: the initial letters of the six words

explanation.surface: A description of high, dry, open country without trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both supplies the letters and describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Veld is the open, largely treeless grassland of the South African plateau, high and dry country.

clue.text: Author knocked back rum, also known as 'Molasses Intoxicator' initially

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so rum is read in reverse
initially means taking the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a playful nickname for rum, which is distilled from molasses

explanation.surface: A writer downed a rum, the drink nicknamed the Molasses Intoxicator.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM 'knocked back' is MUR; then AKA, then 'initially' takes MI from Molasses Intoxicator. 'Knocked back' is a pun: it is also how one drinks rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Haruki Murakami is the Japanese novelist behind Norwegian Wood and Kafka on the Shore.

clue.text: Starters of souvlaki and kofta put before Cypriots regularly in Greek island

indicators.note: starters are the first course, so here the first letters of the two dishes

parts.note: first letters of the two dishes

indicators.note: at regular intervals, every second letter of the word

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Grilled meat starters are served to Cypriot diners on a Greek island holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyros is an island in the Aegean Sea, the largest of the Sporades group off Greece.
